Repository: roboflow/supervision
ITEM #2846
Type: issue
State: open
Title: [Bug]: MeanAverageRecall drops objects with area exactly 32² or 96² from one COCO size bucket (pycocotools and MeanAveragePrecision include them)
Author: user-1
Created: 2026-10-28
Labels: (none)
Body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the issues and discussions and found no similar bug report.

### Bug

**What's the bug?**

`MeanAverageRecall` counts an object whose area is exactly 32² (1024) or 96² (9216) in only one size bucket. pycocotools counts it in both neighbouring buckets. supervision's own `MeanAveragePrecision` also counts it in both, so on the same data mAP and mAR disagree about which bucket an object belongs to.

Why the two disagree:

- **pycocotools:** the size ranges are `[0, 32²]`, `[32², 96²]` and `[96², 1e5²]` ([cocoeval.py#L509](https://github.com/cocodataset/cocoapi/blob/8c9bcc3cf640524c4c20a9c40e89cb6a2f2fa0e9/PythonAPI/pycocotools/cocoeval.py#L509)). An object is excluded only when `area < lo or area > hi` ([#L251](https://github.com/cocodataset/cocoapi/blob/8c9bcc3cf640524c4c20a9c40e89cb6a2f2fa0e9/PythonAPI/pycocotools/cocoeval.py#L251)), so both ends are inclusive.
- **`MeanAveragePrecision`:** uses the same inclusive ranges ([`_OBJECT_SIZE_AREA_RANGES`](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/blob/a87bb76905b631d995049bb5983ce99adfaebd1c/src/supervision/metrics/mean_average_precision.py#L692-L697)).
- **`MeanAverageRecall`:** filters by size in [`_filter_detections_by_size`](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/blob/a87bb76905b631d995049bb5983ce99adfaebd1c/src/supervision/metrics/mean_average_recall.py#L864) through `ObjectSizeCategory`. That uses half-open bins: `area < 32²`, `32² <= area < 96²` and `area >= 96²` ([object_size.py#L131-L133](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/blob/a87bb76905b631d995049bb5983ce99adfaebd1c/src/supervision/metrics/utils/object_size.py#L131-L133)). The mask and OBB variants in the same file work the same way.

The half-open bins in `ObjectSizeCategory` are documented and fine for filtering. The issue is only that `MeanAverageRecall` uses them where COCO semantics are expected.

**Expected behavior:**

Small, medium and large mAR match pycocotools AR, and an object belongs to the same buckets in mAR as in mAP.

**Actual behavior** (perfect prediction on a single box, from the script below):

| box | metric | small | medium | large |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32×32 | pycocotools AR@100 | 1.0 | 1.0 | -1 |
| 32×32 | `MeanAverageRecall` @user-2 | **0.0** | 1.0 | **0.0** |
| 32×32 | `MeanAveragePrecision` | 1.0 | 1.0 | -1 |
| 96×96 | pycocotools AR@100 | -1 | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| 96×96 | `MeanAverageRecall` @user-2 | **0.0** | **0.0** | 1.0 |
| 96×96 | `MeanAveragePrecision` | -1 | 1.0 | 1.0 |

**Who it affects:** any target whose box or mask area is exactly 1024 or 9216. Box-only labels with exact pixel sizes hit this (tiled or synthetic data, fixed-size annotations), and so do integer mask pixel counts. It changes only the small, medium and large mAR values, not overall mAR or mAP. On small datasets, one object moving between buckets is a large change.

**Related, visible in the same output:** when a size bucket has no targets, `MeanAverageRecall` returns `0.0`. pycocotools and `MeanAveragePrecision` return `-1` there, so with mAR "no objects of this size" looks the same as "zero recall". This comes from the [`if not stats:` branch](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/blob/a87bb76905b631d995049bb5983ce99adfaebd1c/src/supervision/metrics/mean_average_recall.py#L497-L510). I'm happy to handle it in the same PR or leave it, whichever you prefer.

**Proposed fix:** have `MeanAverageRecall` select size buckets with the same inclusive ranges as `MeanAveragePrecision`, and leave `ObjectSizeCategory` as documented. Then add boundary parity tests at areas 1023, 1024, 1025, 9215, 9216 and 9217, for boxes and masks, computed with live pycocotools as the [reference parity test guidelines](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/blob/develop/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#reference-parity-tests) ask.

I found this by fuzzing mAP, mAR and keypoint mAP against pycocotools on several thousand random scenes. mAP and keypoint mAP matched everywhere. This boundary case is the only mismatch outside documented behaviour.

### Environment

- Supervision: 0.32.0.dev0 (develop @ a87bb76)
- Python: 3.12.13
- OS: Linux 7.0 (x86-64)
- NumPy: 2.5.4
- pycocotools: 2.0.11

### Minimal Reproducible Example

```python
import contextlib
import io

import numpy as np
from pycocotools.coco import COCO
from pycocotools.cocoeval import COCOeval

import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import MeanAveragePrecision, MeanAverageRecall

for side in (32, 96):  # areas 32**2 = 1024 and 96**2 = 9216, exactly on COCO's thresholds
    box = np.array([[0, 0, side, side]], dtype=np.float32)
    target = sv.Detections(xyxy=box, class_id=np.array([0]))
    prediction = sv.Detections(xyxy=box, class_id=np.array([0]), confidence=np.array([0.9]))

    mar = MeanAverageRecall().update(prediction, target).compute()
    map_ = MeanAveragePrecision().update(prediction, target).compute()

    gt = COCO()
    gt.dataset = {
        "images": [{"id": 1, "width": 200, "height": 200}],
        "categories": [{"id": 1}],
        "annotations": [{"id": 1, "image_id": 1, "category_id": 1, "bbox": [0, 0, side, side],
                         "area": side * side, "iscrowd": 0}],
    }
    gt.createIndex()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
        dt = gt.loadRes([{"image_id": 1, "category_id": 1, "bbox": [0, 0, side, side], "score": 0.9}])
        ev = COCOeval(gt, dt, "bbox")
        ev.evaluate(); ev.accumulate(); ev.summarize()

    print(f"{side}x{side} box (area {side * side}), perfect prediction")
    print("  pycocotools AR@100  S/M/L:", ev.stats[9:12].round(3).tolist())
    print("  sv mAR @100         S/M/L:", [round(float(r.recall_scores[2]), 3) for r in
                                          (mar.small_objects, mar.medium_objects, mar.large_objects)])
    print("  pycocotools AP      S/M/L:", ev.stats[3:6].round(3).tolist())
    print("  sv mAP              S/M/L:", [round(float(r.map50_95), 3) for r in
                                          (map_.small_objects, map_.medium_objects, map_.large_objects)])
```

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [x] Yes I'd like to help by submitting a PR!
